lead: A map of every planet, placed where NASA’s numbers say it is on any date you choose, even back to Aryabhata’s sky in the year 499. Pick a world to see its facts, find out what it would take to send a Starship there, and then try landing on it yourself.
try: Under Pick a world, choose a world such as Mars or the Moon. Then go to Landing trials, press Start descent, and hold Hold to fire to slow down before you hit the ground.
points: Mars’s pull is weaker than Earth’s: a person there would weigh a bit more than a third of what they weigh at home.
Landing on Mars takes less rocket effort than landing on the Moon, even though Mars is much farther away, because Mars’s air does most of the braking.
Earth and Mars both circle the Sun at different speeds, so the distance between them keeps changing: very far apart in 499, much closer on the day of Apollo 11.
